title: Predicting Robot Navigation Outcomes
summary: Machine-learning models that predict whether a robot’s navigation run ends in success, collision, partial completion or timeout.
problem: Given time-stepped sensor and movement logs from autonomous navigation runs, can a model tell how a run will end, and which signals drive that outcome?
approach: We collapsed each run’s time steps into one row (for example, lowest battery level, closest obstacle and whether a collision ever occurred), scaled the features, and compared SVM, k-means, KNN, decision tree and random forest models, sweeping each model’s key parameter and checking 5-fold cross-validation for consistency.
result: Decision trees and random forests were the strongest and most consistent models. Per-run aggregation and feature scaling both made a large difference, and path smoothness and the collision flag carried most of the signal. No model could pick out timeouts, which suggests they depend on factors the dataset doesn’t record.
